adaptation: Raw-byte UTF-8 decoding and quoting in ordinary Rust; source Go printability compiled to sorted disjoint ranges through the existing pinned Genco emitter. No cfg(kani) replacement. The reference package-scoped error prefix is preserved.

shared_utf8_adaptation: Move the existing decoder to one shared owner and spell its source-defined maximum three continuation operations explicitly. Quote hex output is bounded by its maximum eight digits; all source caller widths 2/4/8 and public byte domains remain unchanged. SDK JSON normalization reuses classification with its own replacement policy.
validation: Ordinary full-codepoint category check, all 1111936 valid non-ASCII scalar UTF-8 decodes, 32768 non-ASCII-leading two-byte inputs and boundary witnesses, nineteen independently expected Go/Rust full error strings, and configured consumer error paths preceded the initial gate. The later ASCII property corpus independently checks all 16513 ASCII strings of length zero to two, including all 128 single bytes; it is ordinary evidence and not formal proof. Current metadata correction gates bind both sets without rerunning unchanged production checks.
